judged_text: updateEvent resolves the target calendar with find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate compares against null/undefined, never matches, and calendarId is undefined. Rescheduling a booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId (references created by the new no-credentialId destination branch pass no externalId to createEvent, so result.externalId is undefined) sends the update with an undefined calendarId, the request fails, CalendarManager's catch swallows it, and the booking is rescheduled while the Google Calendar event keeps the old time.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new `updateEvent` calendar resolution is:
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), so it will not match any normal destination calendar and yields `undefined`. This is a concrete logic error introduced by the diff. Separately, the diff also shows paths where `externalId` is not propagated: in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the no-`credentialId` destination branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the new `externalId` argument, and `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns `{ externalId }`, so downstream `result.externalId` can be `undefined` (as the finding describes). Together, this makes the update path prone to failing or targeting the wrong calendar (falling back/defaulting), matching the reported broken reschedule behavior.
